name: Republic Day
notes: National holiday (26 Jan, fixed every year). Long-weekend leisure travel and family visits lift short-haul demand across India.

name: Holi
notes: Festival of Colours (main day; Holika Dahan the evening before). Major domestic travel and family-gathering demand, especially in North India (Mathura/Vrindavan region sees the largest local spikes).

name: Independence Day
notes: National holiday (15 Aug, fixed every year). Long-weekend leisure travel uptick, generally milder than Republic Day/Diwali.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
notes: 10-day festival (Chaturthi to Anant Chaturdashi/Visarjan ~23-25 Sep). Especially strong demand impact in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.

name: Navratri (start)
notes: 9-night festival leading into Dussehra. Strong regional demand lift, particularly Gujarat (Garba/Dandiya) and northern India.

name: Dussehra
notes: Marks the end of Navratri; a major public holiday across India with elevated short-haul and pilgrimage travel demand.

name: Diwali (Lakshmi Puja)
notes: The single biggest demand driver in the Indian festive calendar (5-day festival, main Lakshmi Puja day). Historically the strongest seasonal uplift for travel, hospitality, and retail in India — plan for the largest price/inventory adjustments of the year.

name: Bhai Dooj
notes: Closes the Diwali festival period; smaller, family-visit-driven demand tail after the main Diwali spike.

name: Christmas & New Year Peak
notes: Christmas through New Year's Eve (25 Dec - 1 Jan) is peak leisure travel season in India, especially for hill stations, beach destinations (Goa), and international-style New Year events in metro cities.
